verdict: Ready to merge. It fixes #555 at the cause, using the existing sibling pattern (prose rule over structurally carried row ids, as namesTheFindingsSubject and namesTheEndedOrderDrug already do), and every new write site is pinned by a case that reddens under mutation. The one finding is an ADR paragraph-ordering nit.
what_i_swept: Pass 1: checked the diff stat (15 files, +493/-69, matches). Read the PR body, issue #555, the full production diff and the new tests, plus reference/CLAUDE.md (Matching a drug name, the #260 indexOf rule). Traced the keying of SafetyWarning.partnerRows against namedPartners at every site: the drug-in-play arm (partnerName), the screening arm (chipPartnerName), the merged chip in collapseSharedMechanisms (member partnerName union, built with namedPartners = the same partners list), and interactionWarning's singletonList(partnerName). Every SafetyWarning copy method carries partnerRows (lines 1173/1188/1232/1255/1286 plus withPartnerRows), and the question-pair PairFinding chip names no active order. Checked every RecordMapping construction site, and getFindingPartnerRows reaches no wire (its only consumer is FindingPartnerCoverageCheck). Compared the approach with its siblings namesTheFindingsSubject (ids resolved through getAll(), the same pattern) and namesTheEndedOrderDrug. InteractionClaimPairFidelityCheck already knows her order's display through getFindingBridgeNames, so it is not a missed sibling. Ran CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest, SharedMechanismChipCollapseTest, InteractionClaimPairFidelityTest, FindingPartnerLogDisclosureTest, ArchitectureGuardTest, ProjectInstructionsGuardTest, LlmInferenceServiceTest and OrderStopDateStatementTest: 183 tests, 0 failures. Mutations: (a) disabling the prose-rule arm in statedPartners reddens all four #555 cases (alprazolam on search and searchStreaming, the screen, the merged case), which stands in for fails-on-base, since the new tests cannot compile on base; (b) narrowing the merged chip's rows to the first member reddens the merged case only. Pass 2 (outward): throwaway probes through the real injector, shipped KB and LlmInferenceService. Two prescriptions of one substance (metronidazole tablet+gel, metronidazole 500/250, ketoconazole tablet+cream, fluconazole 150/50, rifampicin 150/300) always produce ONE rule chip named by the KB label, with substance-wide rows, plus a #477 finding with no rows. So the PR's claim that #477's orders are not stated by the bare substance name holds, and the fix also covers dosage-form displays. A shared-alias probe (clopidogrel with omeprazole+esomeprazole orders) raised only an esomeprazole chip, so it could not exhibit the documented alias residue. Swept unchanged prose referring to the check (EndedOrderStatement, the root CLAUDE.md bullet, PatientChartSerializer, README, ADR) for claims made stale; found only the ADR ordering issue. Pass 3: confirmed the incidental test edits are constructor-arity only, and no new findings came up.
could_not_verify: The documented residue (an alias the KB files under two substances names both) through a real pair: my one probe arrangement (clopidogrel; omeprazole + esomeprazole) raised only one rule chip, so I have no concrete example of how often the residue fires.
The issue's dolutegravir question was not reproduced. It is not in the PR's tests, and no live server or LLM was available. By mechanism it should go through the same drug-in-play arm.
No full-repo `mvn clean install`. I ran only the eight related test classes to keep load down on a busy machine.
notes: The new tests cannot compile on base (getFindingPartnerRows does not exist there), so fails-on-base was shown by mutating the prose-rule arm instead. Every probe edit and mutation was restored with git checkout and git status --porcelain is clean. One consistency observation, not raised as a finding: statedPartners unions rows by comparable key across cited findings, so a #477 partner whose printed name equals a rule chip's partner would inherit that chip's rows. My probes showed rule chips print the KB label rather than prescription displays, so I could not construct that collision.
